name: Composite B-Tree Leftmost Prefix
when_to_use: Queries filtering or sorting by multiple columns simultaneously (WHERE tenant_id = ? AND status = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC)
avoid_when: Queries that only search by the secondary column without filtering by the leading column
rules_and_spec: Order columns: 1. Equality filters (tenant_id), 2. Range filters (created_at), 3. Sort columns (id). Leftmost prefix rule applies.
trade_offs: Optimizes multi-clause query speed vs index size and write amplification on INSERT/UPDATE
anti_patterns: Indexing (created_at, tenant_id) when queries filter WHERE tenant_id = 5 (leading column mismatch)

name: Covering Index with INCLUDE
when_to_use: High-frequency latency-critical queries that select 1-3 extra small columns beyond the filter keys
avoid_when: Wide tables with >10 selected columns or large TEXT/JSON columns
rules_and_spec: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user ON orders (user_id) INCLUDE (total_cents, status); Allows Index-Only Scan.
trade_offs: Zero table heap access latency vs wider index leaf pages in memory
anti_patterns: Putting wide text columns into index or INCLUDE clause, inflating index page footprint

name: Partial / Filtered Index
when_to_use: Queries targeting a small subset of rows in a large table (WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' or WHERE deleted_at IS NULL)
avoid_when: Queries that filter across evenly distributed values with no dominant low-cardinality state
rules_and_spec: CREATE INDEX idx_active_tasks ON tasks (user_id) WHERE status = 'PENDING'; Index only contains active rows.
trade_offs: Small memory footprint and fast index updates vs index is ignored if query WHERE clause differs
anti_patterns: Indexing entire 10-million row table when 99% of queries only look at the 5,000 pending items

name: GIN Index for JSONB Search
when_to_use: PostgreSQL tables storing JSONB documents queried using containment (@>) or key-existence (?) operators
avoid_when: JSONB columns that are only retrieved as a blob and never searched or filtered in WHERE clause
rules_and_spec: CREATE INDEX idx_payload_gin ON events USING GIN (payload jsonb_path_ops); Fast containment searches.
trade_offs: Fast JSON search vs GIN indexes are slower to update and larger than standard B-Trees
anti_patterns: Querying WHERE payload->>'user_id' = '123' without an expression index, causing full table scans

name: Expression / Functional Index
when_to_use: Queries filtering on transformed values (WHERE lower(email) = ? or WHERE (first_name || ' ' || last_name) = ?)
avoid_when: Standard queries on raw untransformed column values
rules_and_spec: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_users_email_lower ON users (lower(email)); Enforces case-insensitive uniqueness.
trade_offs: Clean domain ergonomics vs index must match exact expression in query
anti_patterns: Querying WHERE lower(email) = ? when index is on raw email (standard index is ignored)

name: Mandatory Foreign Key Index
when_to_use: Every foreign key column in relational tables (e.g. orders.user_id referencing users.id)
avoid_when: Never avoid; mandatory on all foreign keys
rules_and_spec: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_id ON orders (user_id); Required to prevent table locks during parent deletes.
trade_offs: Small write overhead vs eliminates catastrophic table lock on DELETE/UPDATE of parent rows
anti_patterns: Omitting index on foreign key, causing PostgreSQL/MySQL to execute full table scan or table lock on parent DELETE
